ravi: Bringing up 'harrier-12b:int4p' on canary. Longprefill (24k) shows subtle token drift + increased token repetition starting ~24,580 tokens. Filing here.
zoe: can you share the quick repro and any kv dumps?
ravi: repro: `./ci/run_longprefill --model harrier-12b:int4p --max-tokens 24576 --prompt tests/repro/filler_short.json`
ravi: kvdump around break:
```
[24576] shard1 idx=24576 key=0xcaf0... len=1280
[24577] shard1 idx=24577 key=0xcaf1... len=1280
[24578] shard1 idx=24578 key=0xcaf2... len=1280
[24579] shard1 idx=24579 key=0xcaf3... len=1280
[24580] shard1 idx= -10016 key=0x0000... len=0   <-- suspicious wrap
```
zoe: -10016 is weird; not a plain int16 wrap at 32768. Any pre/post processing that scales/offsets the index?
maria: looks like we do `packed = (idx * posscale_factor) >> shift` in compact path for int4p to fit into int16, then pack. If posscale_factor<1 and rounding is aggressive, the intermediate signed value could underflow when converted back on unpack.
jun: kernel logs show `rot_scale=0.998` on some shards and in the compact path `posscale_factor=0.75` used to reduce dynamic range for fp16->int4 packing.
ravi: so hypothesis: posscale_factor quantization + integer rounding in packing produces a negative pseudo-index near the window boundary which then becomes an obviously invalid idx after unpack -> zeroed kv entry -> generation shift.
zoe: mitigation: two quick things: (1) make packing use saturated arithmetic and detect negative unpacked indices (fail-fast), (2) normalize posscale to 1.0 when running longprefill canaries.
maria: added a small patch: saturated pack/unpack for compact int4 path + debug metric `kv.unpack.invalid_index_count`. PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/7025
ci-bot: [run 2028-01-12T01:05:00Z] scheduled longprefill-harrier (id: 10155)
ci-bot: [workflow] step: collect-kv-dumps
ravi: rerun with patch + posscale=1.0 forced on canary. preliminary: no negative indices at 24.5k and generation matches fp16 baseline through 26k tokens. loss/rouge within noise.
jun: longer term: update onboarding doc: avoid aggressive posscale compression for packing schemes unless you can prove roundtrip safety at target_context*1.5. Also add unit tests that simulate fractional posscale and ensure indices remain monotonic and in-range.
zoe: adding an alert to nightly longprefill: if unpack invalid_index_count > 0 then fail the job and page on-call.
ravi: thanks everyone. I'll run a 48k overnight to stress and report tomorrow. :coffee:
